_README: Two plain sentences per additive: what it is, and what job it does in the food.
These describe the substance and its purpose. They contain no safety judgement -
safety is what the sourced regulator fields on each card are for.
Max 200 characters each. check_cards.py rejects fear words here.

330.what_it_is: A sour-tasting acid found naturally in lemons and limes. The kind used in food is made industrially by fermenting sugar with a mould.
330.why_its_added: Gives a sour taste, keeps colour from fading, and makes it harder for microbes to grow.

322.what_it_is: A fatty substance taken from soya beans, sunflower seeds or egg yolk.
322.why_its_added: Stops oil and water separating, so chocolate, biscuits and mayonnaise stay smooth and even.

322I.what_it_is: A fatty substance taken from soya beans, sunflower seeds or egg yolk.
322I.why_its_added: Stops oil and water separating, so chocolate, biscuits and mayonnaise stay smooth and even.

500.what_it_is: A family of sodium salts. It includes baking soda and washing soda.
500.why_its_added: Makes dough and batter rise, and controls how acidic the food is.

500I.what_it_is: Sodium carbonate, also known as soda ash or washing soda.
500I.why_its_added: Controls acidity and helps baked things rise.

500II.what_it_is: Baking soda, the white powder used in home kitchens.
500II.why_its_added: Releases gas when heated or mixed with acid, so cakes, biscuits and breads rise.

471.what_it_is: Fats broken down into smaller pieces. They can be made from vegetable oil or from animal fat.
471.why_its_added: Keeps oil and water mixed together, so bread stays soft and ice cream stays smooth.

412.what_it_is: A powder ground from the seed of the guar bean, a crop grown widely in Rajasthan and Gujarat.
412.why_its_added: Thickens food and stops the parts of it separating while it sits on a shelf.

415.what_it_is: A thickener made by fermenting sugar with a bacterium, then drying the result into powder.
415.why_its_added: Thickens sauces and drinks, and stops solid bits settling to the bottom.

551.what_it_is: A very fine white powder. It is the same material as sand and quartz, ground extremely small.
551.why_its_added: Keeps powders loose and free-flowing, so salt and spice mixes do not set into lumps.

503.what_it_is: Ammonium salts, an older raising agent that bakers sometimes call baker's ammonia.
503.why_its_added: Makes flat baked things such as biscuits and crackers rise and turn crisp.

503II.what_it_is: Ammonium bicarbonate, an older raising agent also called baker's ammonia.
503II.why_its_added: Makes biscuits and crackers rise and turn crisp.

627.what_it_is: A taste booster. It is usually made by fermenting sugar with yeast, but can come from fish or meat.
627.why_its_added: Makes savoury food taste stronger. It is almost always used together with MSG.

631.what_it_is: A taste booster made from meat or fish, or by fermentation.
631.why_its_added: Makes savoury food taste stronger. It is normally used together with MSG.

211.what_it_is: The sodium salt of benzoic acid, which occurs naturally in cranberries, prunes and cinnamon.
211.why_its_added: Stops mould, yeast and bacteria growing, mainly in sour foods like soft drinks, pickles and sauces.

300.why_its_added: Reacts with oxygen before the food does, so fats stay fresh and cut fruit does not brown.

260.what_it_is: The acid that makes vinegar sour.
260.why_its_added: Adds a sharp taste and makes conditions difficult for bacteria.

319.what_it_is: A man-made antioxidant used in fats and oils.
319.why_its_added: Keeps cooking oil and fried snacks from going rancid and tasting stale.

202.what_it_is: The potassium salt of sorbic acid, which was first found in rowan berries.
202.why_its_added: Stops mould and yeast growing in cheese, baked goods, dried fruit and drinks.

296.what_it_is: The acid that makes green apples taste sharp.
296.why_its_added: Gives a sour taste, mostly in sweets, jellies and drinks.

102.what_it_is: A bright lemon-yellow dye, made in a factory rather than taken from a plant.
102.why_its_added: Colours food yellow. Mixed with a blue dye, it makes green.

110.what_it_is: An orange-yellow dye, made in a factory rather than taken from a plant.

122.what_it_is: A red dye made in a factory. It is also called carmoisine.

133.what_it_is: A bright blue dye made in a factory.
133.why_its_added: Colours food and drinks blue, and is mixed with yellow to make green.

150.what_it_is: A brown colour made by heating sugar until it darkens.
150.why_its_added: Gives food and drinks a brown colour.

150A.what_it_is: A brown colour made by heating sugar on its own, with nothing added.
150A.why_its_added: Gives food and drinks a brown colour.

150D.what_it_is: A dark brown colour made by heating sugar together with sulphites and ammonia.
150D.why_its_added: Gives colas and other dark drinks their brown colour.

101.why_its_added: Colours food yellow, and also puts back a vitamin lost during processing.

375.why_its_added: Put back into flour and cereals to replace what is lost when grain is refined.

407.what_it_is: A thickener extracted from red seaweed.
407.why_its_added: Thickens milk drinks and ice cream, and stops the solid parts settling out.

440A.what_it_is: A natural fibre taken from fruit peel, mostly citrus and apple.
440A.why_its_added: Sets jams and jellies, and thickens fruit drinks.

414.what_it_is: The dried sap of the acacia tree.
414.why_its_added: Stops ingredients separating and carries flavours and colours evenly through a food.

410.what_it_is: A thickener ground from the seeds of the carob tree.
410.why_its_added: Thickens food and stops ice crystals forming in ice cream.

466.what_it_is: Plant cellulose treated so that it dissolves in water.
466.why_its_added: Thickens food and keeps ice cream smooth by stopping large ice crystals.

1442.what_it_is: Ordinary starch, changed slightly so that it holds up to heat, acid and freezing.
1442.why_its_added: Thickens sauces and fillings and keeps them stable after cooking or freezing.

170.what_it_is: Chalk. The same mineral as limestone and marble.
170.why_its_added: Firms food, reduces acidity, adds calcium and whitens.

170I.what_it_is: Chalk. The same mineral as limestone and marble.
170I.why_its_added: Firms food, reduces acidity, adds calcium and whitens.

422.what_it_is: A thick, sweet, syrupy liquid made from fats and oils, which may be from plants or animals.
422.why_its_added: Holds moisture so food stays soft. In slush drinks it also stops the liquid freezing solid.

450.why_its_added: Helps baked goods rise, holds water in meat and fish, and stops discolouring.

450I.what_it_is: A phosphorus salt, also called sodium acid pyrophosphate.
450I.why_its_added: Helps baked goods rise and stops potatoes going grey.

341.what_it_is: A family of calcium and phosphorus salts.
341.why_its_added: Helps baking powder work, keeps powders loose, and adds calcium.

508.what_it_is: A salt much like ordinary table salt, but carrying potassium instead of sodium.
508.why_its_added: Gives a salty taste while putting less sodium into the food.

501.why_its_added: Reduces acidity. It is what makes cocoa powder darker and milder.

331.what_it_is: The sodium salts of citric acid, the acid found in lemons.
331.why_its_added: Controls acidity and keeps processed cheese smooth instead of oily.

282.what_it_is: The calcium salt of propionic acid, which occurs naturally in some cheeses.
282.why_its_added: Stops mould growing in bread and baked goods.

223.why_its_added: Stops dried fruit browning and keeps microbes from growing in juices and some drinks.

320.what_it_is: A man-made antioxidant used in fats and oils.
320.why_its_added: Keeps fats, oils and fried snacks from going rancid.

955.what_it_is: Made from ordinary sugar, changed so the body passes it through. It is around 600 times sweeter.
955.why_its_added: Gives sweetness with almost no calories and without feeding the bacteria that cause tooth decay.

420.what_it_is: A sweet substance found naturally in apples, pears and berries; made industrially from glucose.
420.why_its_added: Sweetens food and holds moisture so it does not dry out.
